items.criterion: The declared accounting divides negative log-likelihood by the raw byte total and not by the token total.
items.judgment: VALUE: bpb_accounting.denominator_basis reads raw_utf8_bytes, and declared_bits_per_byte multiplied by raw_utf8_byte_total reproduces nll_bits_total to 1e-6 relative while the same product over token_total does not, unless the tokenizer is byte-level and the two totals coincide, in which case the distinction is undefined and the identity over the byte total stands alone. The declared number is never read as a score, since graded b comes only from the frozen evaluator; the arithmetic identity is what is graded, and it fails for a pipeline that shrank its token count and called the shrinkage an improvement.

items.criterion: All 256 byte values stay representable, so no held-out byte can arrive as an unknown token.
items.judgment: INVARIANT: the byte-fallback entries <0x00> through <0xFF> are all present in vocabulary.entries. A vocabulary missing even one of them cannot encode the byte that is missing, yet the raw-byte denominator still charges for that byte, so bits per byte collapses on held-out text while every training log looks ordinary.

items.criterion: Each declared byte count is the raw UTF-8 length of the text as it arrived, before any normalisation the pipeline applies.
items.judgment: VALUE: every fixture's raw_utf8_bytes equals the recomputed len(raw_utf8.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')), and bpb_accounting.raw_utf8_byte_total equals the sum of those recomputed lengths. NFKC folding an Arabic presentation form shortens the encoding, so a denominator taken after normalisation is a smaller number over a different corpus and lowers b without teaching the model anything.

items.criterion: The agent says where its wall went, split between encoding the corpus and the fixed-step training run.
items.judgment: EFFECT: agent_budget_declaration parses and names vocab_size, encode_seconds, train_seconds and script_sampling. The declaration is what is graded and not the harness's own measurement, so no field the harness writes can satisfy it; an agent that timed encoding outside the graded region in its own experiments has to say so here, where the omission is visible.

items.criterion: The graded run leaves the frozen trainer, the grading tree and the held-out tree byte-identical.
items.judgment: ABSENCE: run_record.frozen_trainer_digests carries a before and an after map that agree key for key, and guarded_paths_touched is empty. Any change scores 0.0 with reason grading-tree-write or frozen-trainer-modified. Both facts are read from the record the run itself produced, never from a scan taken afterwards, which cannot separate a write made during the graded region from one made before it.

items.criterion: The host-measured graded region fits inside the fifteen-minute wall.
items.judgment: VALUE: run_record.graded_region_wall_seconds, timed from first touch of the training data rather than from interpreter start, is at most 900. Exceeding it scores 0.0 with reason wallclock-exceeded. A vocabulary inflated toward the 65,536 ceiling pays for the inflation in embedding and softmax cost at every one of the 6,000 steps, which turns a defensible compression choice into an exact zero.

items.criterion: Held-out bits per byte, taken as the worse of the two private shards, clears the published bar through the ramp.
items.judgment: EFFECT: b = max(b_P1, b_P2), where each b is the frozen evaluator's total negative log-likelihood in bits over the encoded held-out stream divided by the total raw UTF-8 byte count of the same held-out text. Because the denominator is raw bytes rather than tokens, a tokenizer that shrinks the token count without improving modelling does not move b at all. Lower b is better, so the ramp descends from floor to knee. UNMEASURED AT PHASE 0: the ramp constants are null, so this check raises ConstantUnmeasured rather than returning a score, and the slot is not gradeable until the measurement wave writes them.

items.criterion: Re-executing the declared manifest from a fresh checkout rebuilds the same vocabulary artifact.
items.judgment: EFFECT: run_record.manifest_replay_vocabulary_sha256 equals vocabulary.artifact_sha256. Vocabulary construction is the graded deliverable here rather than a trained model, so the manifest has to reproduce the artifact it claims to have built; a replay that lands on a different digest scores 0.0 with reason manifest-order-divergence.

items.criterion: The submission carries no per-shard bits-per-byte breakdown, no private shard name and no grading constant.
items.judgment: ABSENCE: no key and no string anywhere in the submission matches b_p1, b_p2, shard_p1, shard_p2 or heldout, and no submitted number equals a non-null value in tests/constants.json. The agent surface receives one float and at most one reason code; a per-shard breakdown would expose which of the two disjoint shards is the worse one and let the worse-of-two rule be answered one shard at a time.

items.criterion: The round-trip evidence spans every disclosed adversarial class rather than ASCII alone.
items.judgment: EFFECT: roundtrip_fixtures names all five disclosed classes, arabic_presentation_forms, tatweel, tamil_combining, lone_surrogate and nfkc_unstable, and each carries a non-empty raw_utf8. Identity on ASCII establishes nothing about the shards this slot is graded on, which are Arabic, Devanagari and Tamil as well as Latin.

items.criterion: decode(encode(x)) is byte identity on every fixture the submission carries.
items.judgment: INVARIANT: for each roundtrip_fixtures entry, decoded_utf8 encoded with surrogatepass equals raw_utf8 encoded with surrogatepass, byte for byte. Any difference scores 0.0 with reason roundtrip-not-identity. Losslessness is not a hygiene item here: if encode and decode do not compose to identity, the numerator is measured over a stream that is not the corpus and b is a number about some other text.

items.criterion: The stage order the manifest declares is the stage order the instrumented runner actually executed.
items.judgment: INVARIANT: the stage names of stage_manifest, in declared order, equal run_record.stage_execution_order element for element, every stage carries an entry_point and a sha256, and no stage name repeats. Divergence scores 0.0 with reason manifest-order-divergence, because a manifest that does not describe the run is not a recipe anyone can re-execute.

items.criterion: The pipeline emits its vocabulary, its stage manifest, its round-trip evidence and its byte accounting at the declared submission path.
items.judgment: EFFECT: /submission/c3s1.json parses and carries all four sections: vocabulary, stage_manifest, roundtrip_fixtures and bpb_accounting. A submission missing a section is malformed with reason submission_malformed; it is not a tokenizer that scored badly, it is a tokenizer that was never described.

items.criterion: The 65,536-entry budget is counted off the emitted entry list, never off the number the agent declares beside it.
items.judgment: VALUE: len(set(vocabulary.entries)) is at most 65536 and equals vocabulary.declared_entry_count. Counting the artifact rather than the declaration is the whole point: a declaration that disagrees with the entries it describes scores 0.0 with reason vocab-budget-exceeded, and so does a truthful declaration of an oversized vocabulary.
